newsitem.title: GERMANY: Confectionery exporters fear E.Europe market curbs.
newsitem.headline: Confectionery exporters fear E.Europe market curbs.

text.p: Exporters of confectionery products to eastern Europe fear trade barriers and the rise of domestic production capacity will limit their access to newly emerging markets, a German trade official said on Tuesday.

Bernd Monheim, chairman of the German confectionery industry association BDS, told a news conference many new production facilities were being built up in Hungary, Poland, Romania and the Czech Republic.

Although they were often established in partnership with western manufacturers, they would take away markets from western exporters of finished products which had successfully moved into the region after the collapse of communism.
"Eastern European countries are also becoming increasingly price-conscious and are trying to protect their borders through taxes or other trade barriers," Monheim said.
German exporters would try to maintain and expand their newly-won export markets.
The news conference was organised ahead of the ISM sweets fair, which runs between January 26 and 30.

BDS figures -- only available for January-June 1996 -- showed total German confectionery exports were 383,248 tonnes (up 17.1 percent from January-June 1995), worth 1.85 billion, 15.4 percent more than in the same 1995 period.
Within the total, chocolate exports by volume were up 30.3 percent from a year earlier at 125,034 tonnes and by value up 25.5 percent at 773.3 million marks respectively.
The other categories were biscuits, boiled sweets, ice cream, savoury snacks and instant chocolate drinks.
Most exports went to neighbouring EU countries.
Within the confectionery total, third country exports rose by 24.5 percent to 135,000 tonnes and values increased by 16.2 percent to 620 million marks.
Russia was the leading importer from Germany, taking 60,000 tonnes worth 265 million marks in the first six months alone.
